purpose: Machine-readable entrypoint for agents retrieving Crew Blueprint curriculum, research, citation, evidence, review, lineage, historical-course state, decision context, branch authority, and cross-system context.

research_entrypoints.use: research workflow, source hierarchy, handoff rules
human-readable source and citation master map
normalized evidence graph schema, record families, validator and generated audit views
current research-backed product/content architecture proposal: smaller public course catalog, Field Skills library, guides, advanced Owner Review, and 143-ID reclassification model
machine-readable branch authority/state so historical, archive, exploratory, and active work branches are not mistaken for canonical current state
machine-readable Roadmapdev / Production Atlas / Crew Blueprint utilization graph
normalized reference-first envelope for joining external-system context to Crew Blueprint IDs with provenance, freshness, applicability, allowed use and prohibited inference
whole-system decision substrate separating registered identity, current route, historical content body, evidence/review state, publication state and external authority
42-branch observation scope, historical full-build findings, alternate-presentation rules and catalog-method caveat
current verified external-source updates and next-research candidates for curriculum architecture, safety-awareness freshness, role taxonomy and source monitoring

retrieval_order: Read governance entrypoints and the branch-state registry before substantive work or before consulting non-main branches.

For broad architecture, backlog, restoration or prioritization questions, read course-system-situation-2026-09-06.json and target-audience-content-strategy-and-course-catalog-2026-09-06.md before reasoning from public pages or the 143-ID registry.
Do not interpret course_inventory.jsonl as a command to publish one standalone learner course per registered identity.
Identify the current learner route or domain in course_inventory.jsonl and resolve legacy course IDs through course_id_aliases.jsonl before comparing planned versus built state.
Resolve relevant CONTENT and COMPETENCY relationships through the matrix JSONL tables.
Resolve claim support through SUPPORT_EDGE to SOURCE records; do not infer support from bibliography presence alone.
Check REVIEW, MEDIA, lineage, qualification and supersession state before proposing publication changes.

Consult the all-branch catalog summary and branch-state registry when investigating lost, replaced, archived or alternate course presentations; historical existence is evidence, not automatic restoration authority.
Consult the current research radar for source-freshness and new research priorities; each radar entry is an input, not an accepted learner-facing claim.
Represent cross-system inputs through the cross-system context contract when they need to participate in Crew Blueprint analysis; prefer pointers and provenance over copying volatile source payloads.
Use the ecosystem relationship map only for context owned by another system; do not duplicate volatile external-system data into Crew Blueprint unless explicitly approved.
For analytical prioritization or conflict resolution, consult Roadmapdev; for current employer, vendor, market, union and opportunity context, consult Production Atlas.
Preserve source-system authority and provenance in any derived Crew Blueprint work.

authority_rules.crew_blueprint: canonical for Crew Blueprint curriculum, site state, research matrix and learner-facing publication state
authority_rules.roadmapdev: analytical/intelligence source; recommendations do not become Crew Blueprint truth without accepted Crew Blueprint change
authority_rules.production_atlas: canonical for its current industry, employer, vendor, union, market and opportunity intelligence on its accepted branch
authority_rules.50yearroadmap: canonical for ecosystem governance, relationships and accepted current-state continuity
authority_rules.supabase_roadmap: structured durable state/provenance/current frontier; not a replacement for source-repository canonicality

integrity_expectations: all internal repository paths in this manifest must resolve
matrix references must pass repository validation
cross-system pointers must include repository and canonical ref
cross-system analytical records must preserve source authority, freshness and prohibited inference
volatile external-system data should be referenced rather than copied when possible
course content and evidence lineage must remain distinguishable from analytical recommendations
historical full builds must not be treated as automatically current
research-radar items must remain distinguishable from accepted curriculum claims
non-main branches must not become current truth without an explicit branch-state/owner/governance reason
